claim: For catalogued bases, cub installer output is compared with regular Helm output under recorded inputs.
verify_commands: npm run outcomes:verify; npm run kind-parity:verify; npm run live-parity:verify
limit_or_refusal: The claim is per chart, version, base, values profile, and target profile. It is not a claim over the whole Helm values space.

claim: The top-20 catalog has committed live evidence, but exact strength still depends on the chart, base, and lane.
verify_commands: npm run top20:verify-local-e2e; npm run top20:base-readiness:verify; npm run outcomes:verify
limit_or_refusal: This is not a blanket production-support statement. Production support is target-scoped.

claim: The top-100 corpus contains maintained proof-grade recipe and package artifacts, with readiness separated from production support.
verify_commands: npm run top100:readiness:verify; npm run top100:coverage:verify; npm run next80:verify
limit_or_refusal: Many top-100 rows still need catalog review, useful variants, production disposition, or selected live lanes.

claim: The project maps common Helm pain points to a general solution and per-chart pain reports.
verify_commands: npm run pain-points:verify; npm run catalog:pain-reports:verify
limit_or_refusal: Coverage is strongest for the top-20 and for pain points represented in current source scans and receipts.

claim: Helm hooks and hook-like lifecycle behavior are inventoried and routed to lifecycle receipts, policy, or explicit refusal.
verify_commands: npm run hooks:lifecycle:verify; npm run lifecycle:boundary:verify; npm run lifecycle:gatekeeper-hooks:verify; npm run kps:lifecycle-route:verify; npm run kps:gitops-lifecycle:verify; npm run kps:confighub-lifecycle-promotion:verify; npm run hooks-crds-app:verify
limit_or_refusal: The Kube Prometheus Stack no-crds sequence passed a fresh install and the 85.3.3 to 86.1.0 upgrade through Argo CD and Flux. A separate ConfigHub run retained, approved, promoted, published, and delivered the same upgrade through Argo CD. A person or automation still starts the recorded Job-replacement step. Rollback, long soak, automatic route selection, and other charts need separate proof.

claim: CRDs, webhooks, and controller-populated fields are treated as lifecycle facts that need fresh observation, not as static YAML certainty.
verify_commands: npm run lifecycle:cert-manager-eso:verify; npm run lifecycle:boundary:verify; npm run kps:lifecycle-route:verify; npm run kps:gitops-lifecycle:verify; npm run kps:confighub-lifecycle-promotion:verify
limit_or_refusal: The Kube Prometheus Stack proof covers namespace preservation, CRD ordering, webhook certificate setup, operator-created workloads, and the 85.3.3 to 86.1.0 no-crds upgrade through Argo CD and Flux on kind. Rollback, longer soak, broader migration behavior, and other charts remain separate decisions.

claim: Generated values, existing secrets, and target facts are separated so secret handling is explicit.
verify_commands: npm run redis:verify-package; npm run attack-plan:verify
limit_or_refusal: This does not make ConfigHub a universal secret manager. Some variants require a pre-existing target secret.

claim: Base variants are render-time installer choices; derived ConfigHub variants are post-render refinements for target, environment, region, customer, or operations.
verify_commands: npm run variant-goldens:verify; npm run outcomes:verify
limit_or_refusal: If a change requires a new Helm render, it belongs back in the installer recipe path.

claim: Wrapper chart and values-overlay cases can be modeled as managed imports, with customer choices routed to installer bases or ConfigHub derived variants.
limit_or_refusal: The Kubara-style case is a managed-import pattern, not a free public-catalog guarantee for arbitrary private overlays.

claim: Rendered objects can be scanned, gated, patched, approved, and recorded as ConfigHub operation evidence.
verify_commands: npm run external-scan:verify; npm run scan-disposition:workdown:verify
limit_or_refusal: Scanner results and safe-operation examples do not imply every chart is production-approved.

claim: Selected configurations have live receipts for portable OCI delivery through Argo CD or Flux, with route work and workload health recorded separately.
verify_commands: npm run runtime-gitops:wave:verify; npm run kubara-oci-delivery:verify; npm run sveltos-oci-delivery:verify
limit_or_refusal: Each receipt covers its named package, controller, target, and workload only. Kubara uses one selected service. Sveltos uses two local clusters. Both use temporary registries, so neither is a large production fleet claim.

claim: The command story distinguishes quick inspection, quick ConfigHub import, maintained installer recipes, and post-render variants.
verify_commands: npm run docs:verify; npm run installer:command-surface:verify; npm run variant:command-surface:verify
limit_or_refusal: Fast commands do not carry the same evidence as supported catalog packages unless the proof lanes are run.

claim: A low-friction verified-install path can exist before full paid ConfigHub operations.
limit_or_refusal: This is planning, not a current shipped anonymous service claim.

claim: Signed artifacts, factory scans, image digest inventory, refresh SLAs, private catalogs, and fleet queries are commercial directions.
verify_commands: npm run image-digests:workdown:verify; npm run docs:verify
limit_or_refusal: Security signing and paid support claims require production key, policy, transparency, and SLA decisions.

claim: Blast-radius prediction is scored by comparing predicted affected objects with actual rerender diffs, from committed base pairs and recorded single-value rerender receipts.
verify_commands: npm run blast-radius:accuracy:verify; npm run edges:verify; npm run high-fanout:verify
limit_or_refusal: Measured coverage is still a small slice of the catalog (current counts are in data/blast-radius-accuracy/summary.md). Whole-release identity paths are measured with rename-aware pairing and currently fail, recording that the source maps under-predict them; the route is exhaustive enumeration or a declared whole-release impact scope.

claim: Rendering is recorded as environment-invariant across timezone and locale variations for the measured corpus, per flag profile.
limit_or_refusal: The matrix covers the proof-grade corpus on one operating system, architecture, and helm version; other platforms and helm versions are open columns intended for CI runners. A divergent cell is recorded, not hidden.

claim: Synthetic breaker charts (randomness in selectors, lookup in spec, sprig env, tpl recursion, alias collisions, import-values, verb branching) each land in a named pass, refusal, or route - never silence.
limit_or_refusal: Eight fixtures cover seven outcome classes; the suite grows as breakers arrive. Public problem-chart intake is open, but a reported chart is not supported until it becomes a fixture, receipt, named refusal, or routed gap.

claim: The project refuses to claim that a chart is verified without naming the exact chart, version, base, lane, and target profile.
verify_commands: npm run docs:verify; npm run live-parity:rerun-plan:verify
limit_or_refusal: This is a rule that constrains public claims. It does not reduce the work needed to pass more lanes.
